name: Rechargeable lithium manganese
summary: Rechargeable lithium manganese coin cells, sold with the ML prefix, pair a lithium-aluminum alloy anode with a manganese oxide cathode for 3.0 V nominal. They are charged at a constant 2.8 to 3.2 V and used for memory and real-time clock backup.
body:
## How it works

Panasonic's ML series uses a manganese compound oxide as the positive electrode, a lithium-aluminum alloy as the negative electrode, and a non-aqueous solvent as the electrolyte. Wikipedia lists the Li/Al and manganese dioxide ML cell as a rechargeable lithium metal system at 3 V, mainly marketed by Maxell. The cells are coin format; Panasonic's ML2020, for example, is 20.0 mm in diameter and 2.0 mm high.

## Discharge behavior

Nominal voltage is 3.0 V. Panasonic rates the ML2020 at 45.0 mAh to a 2.0 V cutoff at 20 °C, with a continuous drain of 0.12 mA, so these cells are built for very small currents. The operating range is −20 to 60 °C, and Panasonic gives self-discharge of 2% per year at 20 °C. Cycle life is about 1,000 cycles at 10% depth of discharge relative to nominal capacity.

Charging is constant-voltage. Panasonic's guaranteed charging window is 2.8 to 3.2 V from −20 to 60 °C, with 3.1 V as the standard setting. Panasonic warns that trickle charging of the kind used for nickel-cadmium batteries must never be used, because the cell voltage rises to about 5 V and performance deteriorates. A charge voltage above the specification raises internal resistance, and a charge voltage around 4 V can corrode the positive terminal, which is the case, causing leakage. Below the specification, capacity does not fully recover.

## Uses

Memory backup and real-time clock (RTC) backup in drive recorders, PCs, radio and communication equipment, medical equipment and factory automation equipment, according to Panasonic's ML2020 datasheet. Panasonic Industry Europe also lists tracking and RFID, pagers and memory backup for mobile phones.

## History

Panasonic Industry Europe states that its ML series has been in production for more than 23 years.

## Status

Current. ML is a manufacturer prefix rather than an IEC designation. The digits of the ML2020 match its dimensions, 20.0 mm in diameter and 2.0 mm high.
strengths: About 1,000 cycles at 10% depth of discharge
Higher capacity than VL cells of the same size (ML2020 45.0 mAh against VL2020 20.0 mAh)
limitations: Very low current: 0.12 mA continuous for the ML2020
Needs a constant-voltage charger set between 2.8 and 3.2 V
Cycle life is rated at 10% depth of discharge
safety: Never trickle charge: voltage rises to about 5 V (Panasonic)
A charge voltage near 4 V can corrode the case and cause leakage
Coin format carries the button cell ingestion hazard
